page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top; text in one main column of verse and prose with headings for saints' days; two short parallel columns of verse (left and right) in the lower half. No marginal notes beside the text.

main_text.p: Deus, qui beatam Agnetem, virginem tu- am, caftitatis amore decorafti, & flammis tra- ditam illæfam confervafti, da nobis, quæsu- mus, ejus meritis & precibus, ejusdem casti- tatis tenore fulciri, & ab omni vitiorum æstu liberari.
Et: Apud quem nunc intercedat, ut cœli nobis concedat intrare palatium.
main_text.head: DE S. AGATHA.
5. Februarii.
DE S. DOROTHEA.
6. Februarii.
main_text.p: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, in cujus no- mine gloriosa virgo martyr Dorothea cuncta genera tormentorum superavit, supplicitér te exoramus, ut ejus interventu cuncta peri- cula vincamus, ipsamq; in omnibus necessi- tatibus celerem adjutricem nobis sentiamus.
main_text.head: DE S. APOLLONIA.
11. Februarii.
main_text.l: Virgo Christi egregia | Ne pro reatu criminum,
Pro nobis Apollonia. | Morbo vexemur dentium;
Funde preces ad Do- | Sed sanitate capitis

page.notes: Lower verse block: the left and right columns run side by side; the final lines are partly illegible due to damage at lower right. Catchword and signature not clearly printed; "R3" is a signature-like mark at the foot.
